title: Choose ProofMart's new visual world
question: The roll assigned the Reservation Chart. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. It applies to the whole product: home and security pages, auth, the documents workspace and report, and account.

options.label: Reservation Chart
options.lineage: Indian Railways reservation charts pasted on the coach, and station indicator boards
options.thesis: Every verification is the chart on the coach door: find your row, read its status.
materials: dot-matrix print on tractor-feed continuous stationery
painted coach steel with yellow stencil numbers
options.viewport: Coach-blue steel field with a stencilled headline and a working PDF drop slot on the left. On the right, the sample statement printed as a tractor-feed chart with the disputed row boxed and struck. An LED strip at the top runs the live verdict.
options.risk: Railway theming can read as nostalgic novelty for a B2B trust product. It must stay an information system and never draw a train.

raised.raise: State is a mark, not only a hue: FAIL rows are struck, REVIEW circled, CLEAR ticked, so verdicts survive greyscale print and colour-blindness.
One demand per sheet: each section makes exactly one claim, set at stencil scale.
Step through numbered panels: the developer path (see the document, see the verdict, inspect the evidence, run the API, integrate) is numbered like coach positions, 01 to 05.
Full ink is reserved for the focused finding; the rest of the chart prints at ribbon-worn grey.

options.label: Audit Working Paper
options.lineage: chartered accountants' columnar working papers with red-pencil tickmarks
options.thesis: The report is a CA's working paper: every figure footed, cross-footed and ticked in red pencil.
options.viewport: A full columnar sheet: headline as the sheet title, the sample rows ticked, the broken balance circled with the sum written beside it, and a tickmark legend along the foot.
options.risk: Tops my own list, and sits close to the warm-paper editorial look many runs land on.

options.label: Boarding Pass and Gate Board
options.lineage: airline boarding passes and live departure boards
options.thesis: Each PDF gets a pass; the board reranks verdicts live as results arrive.
options.viewport: A live board of documents ranked by verdict with the changed row held lit, and the sample document's pass with its sha256 as the scannable block.
options.case: Holds product clarity (live rerank maps to webhook results) but loses audience identification to an Indian railway chart.
options.risk: A departure board is a familiar web trope; it needs strict grids to avoid looking like a template.

options.label: Cutting Bench Select Rail
options.thesis: Documents strung as frames on a perforated rail, set-asides hung on pins.
options.viewport: A perforated rail of statement pages across an orange field.
options.case: Lending engineers do not recognise a cutting bench; the rail adds nothing the chart lacks.
options.kept: State is a mark, not only a hue.

options.label: Linocut Broadside
options.lineage: Taller de Gráfica Popular campaign prints
options.thesis: Each claim carved as a single demand.
options.viewport: A gouged block with the claim cut into it.
options.case: Protest-print energy contradicts a calm trust product and hides the evidence.
options.risk: Political register the brand cannot carry.
options.kept: One demand per sheet, at monumental scale.

options.label: Hand-drawn Zine
options.thesis: A friend sketching how forensics works.
options.viewport: Comic panels with a mascot pointing at a boxed row.
options.case: Doodles undercut the precision a reviewer has to defend.
options.risk: Looks unserious next to a FAIL verdict.
options.kept: Numbered panels that step through one hard idea.

options.label: Luminescent Understory
options.thesis: Attention as light in a dark forest.
options.viewport: Glowing growths around a dark document.
options.case: Pure atmosphere; it explains nothing about arithmetic or coordinates.
options.kept: Brightest ink reserved for the focused element.

options.label: Accretion Disk
options.viewport: A warped disk with labels orbiting the rim.
options.case: Spectacle with no link to statements, rows or proof.
options.kept: Lining tabular numerals wherever a figure appears.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark developer-tool landing page: headline, two buttons, and a curl call with its JSON.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and subcopy on the left, a curl request and FAIL response on the right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other API company by design.
